scenarios.title: Harbor City Championship Match
scenarios.place: Fictional East Quay Stadium, Harbor City

map.precision: exercise geometry; not an actual venue
map.editReason: Include fictional rail transfer and riverfront access corridors

observations.claim: A fictional severe-storm warning overlaps the event's planned ingress window.
A fictional bridge approach is closed for scheduled work until 18:00.
Fictional rail service to the transfer stop has a 20-minute delay.
Fictional Gate B is counting arrivals above its exercise planning curve.
The venue's fictional operations desk reports Gate B is intentionally processing two entry lines; no queue spillback is observed.
The fictional utility adapter has not delivered a new status since 12:10.

candidate.summary: Road and rail disruptions may compound ingress pressure if the weather warning remains valid.
limitations: Exercise geometry has no operational precision
Gate B count does not establish a dangerous crowd condition
candidate.nextVerification: Confirm the bridge and transfer-stop service with their fictional operators, then review live venue queue observations.

rejectedCandidate.reason: Gate B arrival count alone suggested crowd distress, but the venue's counter-observation does not support that conclusion.

report.abstract: A fictional storm warning, bridge work and rail delay may complicate entry to the championship match. The available evidence supports an access-planning review, not a confirmed threat or crowd emergency. Gate B throughput is above its planning curve, but the fictional venue desk reports no spillback. Utility status is stale. Operators should verify current bridge, rail and gate conditions before considering a protective action.

scenarios.title: Cross River Heritage Festival
scenarios.place: Fictional River Commons, Northbank and Southbank

observations.claim: A fictional public alert closes a river walkway after a water-main break.
A fictional event partner reposts the walkway closure notice.
The fictional dispatch aggregate is 90 minutes behind the exercise clock.
The fictional issuing office narrows the closure to the south walkway.

candidate.summary: The corrected walkway notice may affect one festival route across two counties.
limitations: Impact on actual pedestrian routing is unverified
candidate.nextVerification: Both fictional county EOCs confirm the revised walkway boundary and publish a consistent route notice.

report.abstract: The fictional issuing office narrowed a walkway closure after its original alert. A partner repost is a duplicate, not independent confirmation. The current record supports a coordinated route check between the two county EOCs; it does not establish a broader public-safety threat.

observations.claim: A fictional venue plan assigns a controlled entrance for the protected-person detail.
A fictional road closure overlaps one planned approach.
A fictional partner message mentions a similar name at another event; identity and presence are unverified.
A fictional advisory names a software product absent from the venue's verified dependency list.

candidate.summary: One planned approach to the fictional event may be affected if the protected-person visit proceeds.
limitations: Unverified name match is not identity evidence
candidate.nextVerification: Detail lead verifies attendance and route status through authorized channels.

report.abstract: A fictional closure intersects one planned approach to the Civic Forum Hall. The exercise protected person is designated, but attendance is not confirmed. A similar-name message and an unrelated cyber advisory do not support an identity or event threat conclusion. The detail lead should verify the approach and attendance through authorized channels.

observations.claim: The fictional assembly permit caps attendance at 1,200 while the organizer estimates 1,800.
Two violent-incident reports appear among 18 comparable fictional evening markets over 24 months; outcomes and exposure hours are unavailable.
The fictional organizer identifies Fictional Market Circuit as promoter and says 600 additional RSVPs came from a repost; promoter history and RSVPs do not establish observed attendance.
The fictional local police liaison acknowledged the event; county EOC and federal awareness are unverified.

candidate.summary: The organizer estimate exceeds the fictional permit capacity; verify the event plan and expected attendance before any resource decision.
limitations: Historical reports do not predict violence at this event
candidate.nextVerification: Contact the fictional organizer and permitting office to reconcile capacity, footprint and controls.

report.abstract: The fictional night market has an issued assembly permit for 1,200 people and an organizer estimate of 1,800. This mismatch warrants an event-management review. Two historical violent-incident reports from 18 comparable fictional markets provide limited context and do not predict violence here. Sound approval is pending, temporary-structure status is unknown, and no federal resource request has been sent.
